text: Applied to a case of the human will, a determinist would argue that the will does not have causal power and that something outside the will causes the will to act as it does.
subject: something outside the will

text: However, deontology also holds not merely the positive form freedom (to set ends freely) but also the negative forms of freedom to that same will (to restrict setting of ends that treat others merely as means, etc.).
subject: freedom

text: David Hume, as part of his opposition to rationalism, argued that pure reason alone cannot prove the reality of efficient causality; instead, he appealed to custom and mental habit, observing that all human knowledge derives solely from experience.
subject: human knowledge

text: Incompatibilism holds that determinism is incompatible with free will, so if determinism is true, "free will" does not exist.
subject: determinism

text: Compatibilism, on the other hand, holds that determinism is compatible with, or even necessary for, free will.
subject: determinism

text: Functionalism is a position in modern philosophy of mind that holds that we can define mental phenomena (such as beliefs, desires, and perceptions) by describing their functions in relation to each other and to the outside world.
subject: mental phenomena

text: Because a computer program can accurately represent functional relationships as relationships between symbols, a computer can have mental phenomena if it runs the right program, according to functionalism.
subject: computer

text: Computationalists and functionalists reject A3, arguing that "syntax" (as Searle describes it) can have "semantics" if the syntax has the right functional structure.
subject: syntax

text: Coherentism claims, at a minimum, that not all knowledge and justified belief rest ultimately on a foundation of noninferential knowledge or justified belief.
subject: knowledge

text: Coherentists typically hold that justification is solely a function of some relationship between beliefs, none of which are privileged beliefs in the way maintained by dogmatic foundationalists.
subject: justification

text: Foundationalism relies on the claim that it is not necessary to ask for justification of certain propositions, or that they are self-justifying.
subject: Foundationalism

text: Coherentists argue that this position is overly dogmatic.
subject: dogmatic position

text: But, unlike the relativist, the coherentist argues that these associations may be objectively real.
subject: associations

text: Coherentists therefore argue that the only way to reach proof-theoretic truth that is not relativistic is through coherency.
subject: proof-theoretic truth

text: === Coherentism's response === Coherentism rejects the soundness of the regression argument, which assumes that the justification for a proposition follows a linear sequence: P" justifies P', which in turn justifies P.
subject: Coherentism

text: According to coherentism, justification is a holistic process.
subject: justification
